memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Jacob left Beersheba, and Israel's sons took their father Jacob and their children and their wives in the carts that Pharaoh had sent to transport him. So Jacob and all his offspring went to Egypt, taking with them their livestock and the possessions they had acquired in Canaan. Jacob brought with him to Egypt his sons and grandsons and his daughters and granddaughters—all his offspring." — Gen 46:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Picture the caravan. Old men, small children, wives, herds, carts, bundles — an entire clan pulling up its roots and moving to a foreign country. Nobody is left behind. Sons, grandsons, daughters, granddaughters: the text lingers on the completeness of it.

This is a family that nearly destroyed itself. Jealousy, deception, a brother sold, a father lied to, two decades of silent grief. By all reasonable expectation this family should have splintered permanently. Instead here they are, travelling together, whole.

Only God does that. Reconciliation of this depth is not a natural outcome; it is a work of grace over years.

And notice that they travel in Pharaoh's carts — the very evidence that had revived Jacob's spirit. What convinced him is now what carries him. God often gives us both the reason to believe and the means to obey.

There is something quietly hopeful here for anyone with a fractured family. God has restored worse. The story of Scripture is one of God gathering people who scattered themselves — and in Christ He gathers a family from every nation into one household (Eph 2:19).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where in your family is God's work of reconciliation still needed?
2. Has God given you both a reason to trust Him and the means to obey?
3. Who might God be asking you not to leave behind?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You restore what looks beyond repair. Do that work in my family and in my relationships, and give me patience for the years it may take. Amen.
